newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch retailer Beter Bed to make bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: Dutch retailer Beter Bed to make bourse debut.

text.p: Bedroom furniture retail chain Beter Bed will make its debut on the Amsterdam stock exchange on December 5, ABN AMRO bank said on Monday.
Beter Bed will issue just over four million shares at a price of 25 to 28 guilders each in an initial public offering, with the definitive price being announced on December 5.

Beter Bed is the Netherlands' biggest bedroom furniture chain, operating 52 outlets under its own name and a further nine under the name of its former upmarket rival Dormael, which it took over earlier this month.
In the first half of 1996 Beter Bed's sales rose 22.2 percent to 70.9 million guilders while net profit climbed 20 percent to 6.0 million guilders.
For the whole of 1995 Beter Bed's net profits rose 34 percent to 8.7 million guilders while sales were 22 percent higher at 118 million guilders.
The company's earnings are usually lower in the second half of the year than in the first.
Founded 15 years ago by Mark and Pieter Diks, Beter Bed focuses on the middle segment of the Dutch bedroom furniture market.
The company has said a bourse listing will give it freer access to the capital market to finance further expansion.
The recent acquisition of Dormael reflects the firm's ambitions to move into the upper segment of the market. In the longer term Beter Bed also plans to expand abroad.
In addition to its retail outlets the company also owns two furniture production units in Poland and one in the Netherlands.
